title: Construct initial Fisher growth without taking an infinite-ion final model
statement: Use h_sigma(r)=Z^-1 exp[-(r^2-1)^2/sigma^2], cutoff chi supported(1/2,3/2), chi=1 on[3/4,5/4], a0=chi r^(3/2),Y(omega)=omega1 and f_epsilon=Z_epsilon^-1 h_sigma exp(epsilon a0 Y). It is strictly positive Schwartz and unperturbed near the origin. For angular L=div(P_v/|v| grad)=r^-3 Delta_S2, Fisher variation equals -16pi epsilon^2/3 int h_sigma r^-3[(r a0prime-3a0/2)^2-a0^2/4]dr+O(epsilon^4); the integral tends to -1/(16pi). Choose sigma then epsilon to make it positive. Replace the point background by a FIXED Gaussian g_delta: unsplit variation Psi_f=-2Delta log f-|grad log f|^2 and the continuous bounded tensor convolution justify A_delta->A0>0. With fixed f,g, m1=1,m2=M,c11=c22=1,cross c, define finite S,A,B,C,D as in the source. EXACT I_mprime(0)=S+cA-cB/M-cD/M^2+cC/M^3. Choose c=(|S|+1)/A,K=|B|+|C|+|D| and FINITE M>max(1,2cK): derivative>1/2. This extends the auxiliary frozen-background mechanism to an admissible finite-mass initial functional example. It is not solution blowup, global-Cauchy failure or a novelty claim for the already-known angular seed.
